_doc: Upsell hot keys: words and phrases that force the upsell to be re-evaluated the moment
they are heard. One list for every consumer: the demo POS's Vavoom Assist reads it
(hotkeys.js), and whisper can load the same file when hot keys go live, so the patterns
use only regex syntax that JavaScript and Python share (\b, groups, alternation, ?).
Patterns are matched case-insensitively against one transcript line. `unless` patterns
veto a match in the same line. `effect` is what the upsell does (see hotkeys.js).
`evidence` is how often the family occurs in real Starbucks Downtown speech: share of
143 full conversations (2026-08-13..17) and of 1,730 short voice clips (2026-09-08..10-03).
Speaker labels in that data bleed between operator and customer, so no hot key depends
on who said it; the wording carries that (an operator says 'we're out of').
`timing_rules` holds rules that are not phrases (the 3-second patience rule), applied by useAssist.js.
On the demo POS these are the upsell engine's guidelines: a hot key's response outranks basket completion, the AI's pick and screen behaviour (upsellEngine.js).

`skip_in_item_names`: the key does not fire on words that are part of a menu item the line names ("a veggie sandwich" is the order, not a customer open to food; David, 2026-10-08). The POS's hotkeys.js honours it; the GPU-side readers (the demopos brain and meaning layer) ignore it, and neither acts on Wants food.

hotkeys.label: Item out of stock
hotkeys.meaning: Something the customer asked for, or Vavoom was about to pitch, can't be sold right now
hotkeys.action: Never offer that item again today; pop up the closest substitute at once, tagged Closest substitute

hotkeys.label: Asked if we have something
hotkeys.meaning: Interest in a specific item, often one they can't see on the menu board
hotkeys.action: Pitch the item with a complementary item below it; if we're out of it or don't carry it, the closest substitute

hotkeys.label: Complaint (order problem)
hotkeys.meaning: Something about the order went wrong
hotkeys.action: Stop pitching for a minute; fix the order first

hotkeys.label: Too sweet
hotkeys.meaning: Finds it, or the last one, too sweet
hotkeys.action: Offer something to counter it: plain, unsweetened or savoury, tagged Counter: too sweet

hotkeys.label: Too bitter
hotkeys.meaning: Finds it, or the last one, too bitter
hotkeys.action: Offer something to counter it: something sweet, tagged Counter: too bitter

hotkeys.label: Doesn't like it
hotkeys.meaning: Doesn't like an item (the one named, or the last one ordered)
hotkeys.action: Offer an alternative from the same category, tagged Alternative

hotkeys.label: Took forever
hotkeys.meaning: The wait was too long
hotkeys.action: If the menu has a souvenir, offer it free, tagged Complimentary

hotkeys.label: Dairy-free
hotkeys.meaning: Avoids dairy (allergy, intolerance or diet)
hotkeys.action: Drop milk, cream, cheese and shake pitches; dairy-free add-ons only

hotkeys.label: Watching sugar
hotkeys.meaning: Watching sugar
hotkeys.action: No sweet treats or syrup-heavy pitches; savoury or unsweetened add-ons

hotkeys.label: No caffeine
hotkeys.meaning: Avoids caffeine
hotkeys.action: No extra shots, espresso or cold-brew pitches

hotkeys.label: Health-minded
hotkeys.meaning: Choosing on health
hotkeys.action: Prefer protein and lighter add-ons; no indulgent treats

hotkeys.label: Going large
hotkeys.meaning: Not price-led; big appetite or a long day ahead
hotkeys.action: Premium add-ons welcome

hotkeys.label: Price-conscious
hotkeys.meaning: Price matters
hotkeys.action: A size-up said as "only $X more"; low-priced add-ons framed as value

hotkeys.label: Paying with stars or a card
hotkeys.meaning: Part of the order is already paid for, so the customer feels ahead
hotkeys.action: Pitch a paid food add-on alongside the redeemed drink

hotkeys.label: Ordering for others
hotkeys.meaning: More than one person is being served
hotkeys.action: Basket completion: a second item for the other person, not a bigger cup

hotkeys.label: Regular order
hotkeys.meaning: A habitual order; they know what they want
hotkeys.action: Don't swap the drink; add something to the usual

hotkeys.label: Seasonal interest
hotkeys.meaning: Responding to the season's menu
hotkeys.action: Pair with a seasonal food or treat when the menu has one

hotkeys.label: Wants food
hotkeys.meaning: Open to food
hotkeys.action: Pitch food before drink add-ons

hotkeys.label: Drink only
hotkeys.meaning: Has said no to food
hotkeys.action: No food pitches; a drink upsize or add-in only

hotkeys.label: In a hurry
hotkeys.meaning: In a hurry
hotkeys.action: Shorten or skip the pitch; only something ready to hand

hotkeys.label: Needs a boost
hotkeys.meaning: Low on energy
hotkeys.action: Extra shot or a size up

hotkeys.label: Feeling hot / hot weather
hotkeys.meaning: The customer feels hot, or says it is hot out
hotkeys.action: Pop up the most-ordered cold item, tagged Something cold, unless a cold drink or shake is already on the ticket; iced and cold items rank higher

hotkeys.label: Feeling cold / cold or wet weather
hotkeys.meaning: The customer feels cold, or says it is cold or wet out
hotkeys.action: Pop up the most-ordered warm item, tagged Something warm, unless a hot drink is already on the ticket; hot drinks and warm food rank higher

hotkeys.label: Wants something cold
hotkeys.meaning: The customer asks for something cold or refreshing
hotkeys.action: Pop up the most-ordered cold item (a drink first), tagged Something cold, unless a cold drink or shake is already on the ticket; cold items rank well above hot ones

hotkeys.label: Wants something hot
hotkeys.meaning: The customer asks for something hot or warming
hotkeys.action: Pop up the most-ordered warm item (a hot drink first, else warm food), tagged Something warm, unless a hot drink is already on the ticket; hot items rank well above cold ones

hotkeys.label: Undecided
hotkeys.meaning: Wants a recommendation
hotkeys.action: One clear recommendation: the bestseller

hotkeys.label: Order closing
hotkeys.meaning: The order is about to close
hotkeys.action: One last small add-on now, then stop

timing_rules.label: Not patient
timing_rules.rule: The customer's first order line comes within 3 s of the customer walking up (counter presence opened the session). Not judged when a greeting, a tap, Start or the order itself opened it: answering the greeting within 3 s is the normal pace.
timing_rules.action: Short pitch only: a quick size-up or a cheap ready item first
